rejected.rationale: Reviewer confirmed the negative-control test IS failure-capable (reverting recoverView to nullary turns it red) and could not make it pass for a wrong reason. Its redundancy with the inline guard is deliberate: the orchestrator required a permanent, named guard proving the parity assertion cannot silently go vacuous again. The inline guard protects the forwarding; the named test states the obligation and is the artifact a future reader greps for. Keeping both is the point, not an oversight. The reviewer's alternative suggestion — extend it to the production adapter path — is real but is the FND-004 gap, which is now recorded as gate G1 rather than built here (out of scope per orchestrator).
